info.title: Fenergo Nebula Screening Command
info.description:
**Screening Command API**:
Screening Command API screens clients and their associated parties for adverse media, PEP and sanctions. Use Screening Command API to perform the screening action and Screening Query API to retrieve screening results.
**Screening Command API provides**:
  • The ability to screen Individual and Company Legal Entities.
  • The ability to trigger asynchronous screening requests to different providers.
  • The ability to screen multiple entities in a single request.

post.summary: Create a new screening batch to screen one or more entities
post.description:
• This method creates a screening batch that triggers asynchronous requests to different screening providers.
  • This batch ID can be used in the Screening Query Api to check the status of the request and to get the screening results.
  • The method returns the batch ID created in the system.
  • For Individuals, the mandatory fields are; tenant + fullName + type OR tenant + firstName + lastName + type.
  • For Company’s, the mandatory fields are tenant + type + LEName.
  • If providers is null the batch will be created with the active providers.
  • If configuration set is null the batch will be created for the specified provider with the default configuration set.
  • Otherwise the batch will be created with the providers and configuration sets specified in the request.

Following permissions are required: ScreeningCreate, ScreeningAccess

post.summary: Creates new Screening entities in bulk
post.description:
This method is used to create multiple Screening entities at once in a single request. Pre-requisites: The 'legalEntityId' supplied for each entity as part of the request should already exist in Fen-X. Considerations: Each entity in the request is managed as an independent operation. This means that some of the requests may be successful and some of them may not. Therefore, it is important to review the properties 'numberOfEntitiesCreated' and 'numberOfEntitiesFailed' in the response of the endpoint. This will give a general view of the outcome of all the operations submitted. In addition, the 'status' property of the response will provide the status of each operation, and the 'errorMessage' property will tell the reason why the operation failed. There is a maximum number of entities that can be submitted in a single request. If you hit that limit, please split the entities in multiple requests and try again.

Required permissions:
Following permissions are required: ScreeningCreate, ScreeningAccess
